passage: Our exams ran from the fourth to the fourteenth, and I watched Chaitanya prepare like someone laying bricks. A week before, he pinned a calendar above his desk: heavy days shaded red, one blank Sunday, and the four days after the last paper marked "nothing". During the exams he studied until ten and then switched off his lamp, even while the rest of us were still panicking in the corridor. On the blank Sunday he played football and came back muddy and hungry. When the exams were over, he slept, cooked with his mother and only opened a book on the fourth day, lightly. I cannot say what he was thinking. But he was the only one of us who walked into the last paper looking awake, and the only one who was not ill afterwards. Uma

qa.q: What did Chaitanya mark on the calendar for the four days after the last paper?
qa.a: The four days after the last paper were marked "nothing".

qa.q: What might Chaitanya have been feeling when he switched off the lamp at ten while others panicked?
qa.a: Probably calm and confident in the plan, though Uma cannot be sure and only saw the behaviour.

qa.q: What could a panicking friend learn from Chaitanya's calendar?
qa.a: Plan the hard days with rest days around them, and put recovery on the calendar before the exams begin.

qa.q: How might Uma have felt watching the others panic while Chaitanya switched off the lamp?
qa.a: Probably a mix of admiration and envy, since Uma noticed Chaitanya looked awake and was not ill afterwards.

grounding: Illustrates a student who accepts an intense exam phase but schedules rest before and after it, seen by a classmate.

passage: On Tuesday, Sahil drew two columns on the whiteboard for the college fest. "Sprint for the last ten days, then a slow week after," he told Wasim, his co-organiser, and he blocked the Monday after the fest as a holiday for the whole team. On the Friday of fest week, Sahil ran the stage checks until midnight, went to bed at one, and refused Wasim's offer to stay until three. "Tomorrow is the real day. Be in by eight." The following Wednesday, the volunteers sat in the canteen at four o'clock, laughing and doing nothing. Sahil had answered only two messages all week, and Wasim finally had time to fix the banner properly, unhurried. "We'll do the same next term," Sahil said, tapping the whiteboard, where the slow week was still written in green.

qa.q: What did Sahil block as a holiday for the whole team?
qa.a: Sahil blocked the Monday after the fest as a holiday for the whole team.

qa.q: What was Sahil probably feeling when he refused to let Wasim stay until three?
qa.a: Calm and protective of the team's energy, wanting everyone fresh for the real day.

qa.q: What did the plan get right about the last days before a big event?
qa.a: It put the hard push into a short window and set a recovery week after it, so the team could repeat the effort next term.

qa.q: How might Wasim have felt on the Wednesday with time to fix the banner unhurried?
qa.a: Relieved and rested, able to do the work properly rather than rushing while tired. 😊

grounding: Illustrates a thoughtful organiser who plans an intense phase for an event and a planned recovery week afterwards.
